ops.title: PPR retrieval lane: kill test retired, lane kept — the eval cannot arbitrate a 2ms decision
ops.body:
Decision (2026-07-29, yasyf): KEEP the personalized-PageRank retrieval lane and RETIRE
the plan's Phase 2 kill test. This reopens a pre-committed exit, deliberately: that clause
assumed a costly lane and an eval that could arbitrate it, and both premises are falsified.

WHY THE EXIT WAS REOPENED

Cost, now measured, was never the issue: the PPR lane is ~2ms/query and +6-13% index build.
The graph build itself (~2.7s) is paid for by anchor enrichment regardless, which stays.
Spending ~1 day of Go plus re-authoring ~40 questions to decide about 2ms is a bad trade.

THE TWO RUNS

Run 1 (2026-07-28, defective instrument). Trigger fired: lexical-alone recall@10 = 0.910
vs the 0.60 bar. Graph marginal +0.038 NDCG, CI [-0.006,+0.083], sign p=0.58, below the
0.062 MDE. Verdict was DELETE_PPR — overturned, because two refuters found the eval never
set rank.Options.Session, the configuration internal/cli/kg.go sets on every real query.

Run 2 (2026-07-29, rebuilt instrument: frozen corpus, session context on eval.Question,
112 questions, permutation/Wilcoxon, held-out split). Verdict STILL_UNDERPOWERED, high
confidence. Trigger fired again at recall@10 = 0.747. Run 1's claimed session inversion
DID NOT REPLICATE: with Session threaded, monorepo is +0.0636 (best row in the ablation,
+0.0652 held out), four small repos negative.

WHY IT CANNOT BE DECIDED ON THIS INSTRUMENT

Every decision-carrying contrast sits below its own 80%-power MDE (monorepo 0.0636 vs
0.0812; held-out 0.0652 vs 0.0843; pooled 0.0207 vs 0.0731). Smallest p anywhere is 0.0291
against a Holm bar of 0.0028 for the 18 cells scanned; an all-null scan yields a p that
good 41% of the time.

Two instrument defects the rebuild itself introduced or exposed, both unfixed:
- SESSION-LABEL CONTAMINATION: 37/100 sessions carry a path in the gold record's own
  anchor set (placebo 0.93%, 40x enrichment). The pooled session-arm gain lives entirely
  in that subpopulation (+0.1018 vs -0.0269). Verified NOT to explain the monorepo result.
- POOLING LAUNDER: tune.go keys the held-out pool by arm only while w=0.00 is a bit-exact
  no-op with Graph=true, so four repos whose sweeps chose "lane off" enter the only pooled
  CI excluding zero as null-treatment ties.

THE CASE AGAINST KEEPING, recorded because it is strong

The trigger fired twice (0.910, then 0.747). The tuner votes w=0 in 4 of 12 arm-repo
combinations. Each instrument fix SHRANK the effect (+0.038 -> +0.021 pooled). At k=3,
where the plan's own reframe says value must live, the marginal is +0.003 to +0.008. Three
rounds of shrinking, non-robust, conditionally-positive readings are what a true null
looks like.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT

Pre-registered hypothesis for anyone with a reason to revisit: cross_branch is where the
lane wins if it wins anywhere (recall 0.929 -> 1.000; multihop +0.076). Treat that as the
sole primary, not as a post-hoc subgroup — an all-null category scan produces a result
that good ~27% of the time. A decision-grade instrument needs: cross-fitted folds
(doubles held-out n free), the w=0 pooling fix, a within-repo session-permutation control
arm, the 37 contaminated sessions re-authored blind to gold, ~40 more monorepo questions,
and a pre-declared minimum effect of interest. NDCG@3 + leak@3 arbitrate, not recall@10 —
recall@10 is at ceiling here and measures what the plan's reframe disavows.

The deletion diff is preserved at
~/.claude/projects/-Users-yasyf-Code-cc-notes/ppr-deletion.patch (208 insertions / 970
deletions; deletes graph.go and fusion.go, keeps kg.Build and anchor enrichment).
